title: Where A Small Language Model Helps in Invoice Categorisation, Understood Through Embedding Geometry
abstract: arXiv:2608.18033v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Categorising invoices into the correct General Ledger (GL) code underpins financial reporting and tax compliance. This is a skilled accounting judgement rather than a routine task: the correct category depends subtly on the nature of the purchasing business, the vendor and the invoice text. Whilst AI is increasingly being adopted across industries to automate tasks, including invoice categorisation, implementations built on in-house small language models (SLMs) can simultaneously reduce cost and improve data security, confidentiality, and interpretability. We investigate this approach by first analysing the pre-trained embedding geometry of a small sentence transformer (SBERT) and classic SLM (DeBERTa). translated_title: 小型语言模型在发票分类中的辅助作用：通过嵌入几何理解
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.18033v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：将发票正确分类为总账（GL）代码是财务报告和税务合规的基础。这是一项需要专业会计判断的任务，而非例行工作：正确的类别取决于采购业务的性质、供应商和发票文本的微妙差异。尽管人工智能在各行业中被越来越多地采用以自动化任务（包括发票分类），但基于内部小型语言模型（SLM）的实现可以同时降低成本并提高数据安全性、机密性和可解释性。我们通过首先分析小型句子变换器（SBERT）和经典SLM（DeBERTa）的预训练嵌入几何来研究这种方法。该财务语料库的句子嵌入空间在全局上是各向异性的，但由局部各向同性的簇组成，将先前的词级发现扩展到金融环境中的句子嵌入，并且这些簇强烈地...
tldr: 该论文通过分析小型语言模型在金融发票文本中的嵌入几何结构，揭示了全局各向异性但局部各向同性的簇状分布，从而证明了小型语言模型在发票分类中既能降低成本、提升安全性，又能保持可解释性。
en_tdlr: This paper analyzes the embedding geometry of small language models on financial invoice text, revealing globally anisotropic yet locally isotropic cluster structures, demonstrating that SLMs can reduce cost, enhance security, and maintain interpretability in invoice categorization.
